selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: In the comparison, how much money did the first servant get?
questions.answer: He got twenty gold pieces.

questions.question: In the story, why was twenty gold pieces enough for the first servant?
questions.answer: Because it was enough to buy very good clothing.

questions.question: Why was the second servant’s money not meant for the same simple use?
questions.answer: Because it was a much larger amount and came with instructions.

questions.question: What should the second servant have done before spending the money?
questions.answer: He should have read the paper.

questions.question: What does this tell us about following others without thinking?
questions.answer: It can lead to foolish choices.

questions.question: How did his suit compare with the first servant’s suit?
questions.answer: It was much worse.

questions.question: How did the employer react to the second servant’s choice?
questions.answer: He scolded him and punished him.

questions.question: What should people not use their life’s gifts for?
questions.answer: They should not use them only for physical enjoyment.

questions.question: Are humans said to have less or more capital than animals?
questions.answer: They are said to have more.

questions.question: What is the big idea of this comparison?
questions.answer: Human abilities were not given just to chase worldly life.

questions.question: What was special about the cloth for the first servant’s clothes?
questions.answer: It was a certain cloth chosen for him.

questions.question: What did the master tell the first servant to do with twenty gold pieces?
questions.answer: To get a suit made.

questions.question: What does the written note tell us?
questions.answer: It shows he had an important task or business to do.

questions.question: What did the second servant do wrong before going to the shopkeeper?
questions.answer: He failed to read the instructions.

questions.question: What was the result of his bad choice?
questions.answer: He wasted the money and got bad clothing.

questions.question: Why was the master right to be upset?
questions.answer: Because the servant wasted what was given and did not do his real job.

questions.question: What kind of life are we told not to live?
questions.answer: A life only for fleshly pleasure and temporary things.

questions.question: Why is the warning stronger for human beings than for animals?
questions.answer: Because humans have been given greater gifts and abilities.

questions.question: What does the passage say we should understand from the story?
questions.answer: That our human powers are for more than animal-like living.

questions.question: Did the first servant succeed in getting good clothes?
questions.answer: Yes, he got fine clothes.

questions.question: What else was put in the second servant’s pocket?
questions.answer: A paper with instructions.

questions.question: Instead of thinking carefully, whom did the second servant copy?
questions.answer: He copied the other servant.

questions.question: What does the poor suit show about his decision?
questions.answer: It shows his decision was careless and foolish.

questions.question: Did the second servant get better clothes than the first servant or worse clothes?
questions.answer: He got worse clothes.

title: Warning to the Wicked and the Self Explanation of Misuse Through a Parable and Awakening the Self
